value.name: Daniel orders Lucia to read letter
value.description: Daniel insists that Lucia read the letter aloud instead of reading it himself.
evidence: "Read it," he said.
"Daniel."
"Read it."

value.name: Lucia reads letter aloud
value.description: Lucia reads the letter carefully and without embellishment, including the parts about Daniel.
evidence: Lucia read the letter out loud.
She read it carefully and without performance.
She did not skip the parts about him.

value.name: letter reveals mother's apology
value.description: The letter explains that Daniel will be hurt, that the mother hoped Lucia would be patient, and that she was sorry for not telling him herself.
evidence: She knows Daniel will be hurt.
She knows Daniel has carried the idea of this house in him for a long time.
She hopes Lucia will be patient with him.
She says she is sorry she did not tell him herself.
She says she was a coward about it.
She says, at the end, please forgive me, both of you, for not being braver.

value.name: silence follows the reading
value.description: After Lucia finishes the letter, the room falls silent for a long time.
evidence: When Lucia finished, no one spoke for a long time.

value.name: Daniel confesses finding hidden note
value.description: Daniel admits that he found a handwritten note in his mother's desk the day after she died.
evidence: Then Daniel said, very quietly, "I found a piece of paper. In her desk. The day after she died."

value.name: Daniel reveals codicil location note
value.description: Daniel explains that the paper was a note telling where the codicil was hidden behind the bobbins in the sewing machine.
evidence: "It was not the codicil," he said.
"It was a note in her handwriting. It said where the codicil was. It said, behind the bobbins in the sewing machine."

value.name: Daniel destroys the note
value.description: Daniel puts the note in his pocket, then burns it in the bathroom sink and runs water until it is gone.
evidence: I read it. I put it in my pocket. I went upstairs and I burned it in the bathroom sink and I ran water until it was gone.

value.name: Daniel admits avoiding the codicil
value.description: Daniel says he never checked behind the bobbins because he did not want to know whether the codicil existed.
evidence: "I did not look behind the bobbins," he said.
"I did not want to know if it was there."

value.name: Daniel rationalizes denial
value.description: Daniel explains that he convinced himself the note was meaningless and that his mother had not really done it.
evidence: "I told myself if I did not look, it did not exist."
"I told myself the note was nothing. A scrap. A draft."
